title: Screen locker takes a second of black screen to activate
line: Locking keeps the desktop on screen until the lock screen is ready, instead of showing a black screen while it starts.
explanation: When the session locks, KWin hides every window but the lock screen at once, and the screen stays black until a freshly started kscreenlocker_greet has loaded its QML and drawn its first frame (0.4-1 s). KWin now pauses the outputs' render loops when the lock starts, so the last desktop frame stays on screen (input already goes only to the locker), and resumes them as soon as a lock screen window is mapped, on unlock, when the system is about to sleep, or after 2 s.

commits.message:
wayland: keep the last frame on screen until the lock screen shows

Locking turned the screen black until the greeter had drawn its first
frame, up to a second later. Pause the outputs instead until a lock
screen window appears, the session unlocks or the system sleeps (≤2 s).

BUG: 520995

review.text: The patch hides the greeter's startup latency in KWin instead of fixing it: it freezes every output on the last unlocked frame for up to 2 s after KSldApp reports the session as locked, so anything on screen stays visible while ksld, logind and ScreenSaver.ActiveChanged already say it is hidden. That breaks the guarantee KWin blanks for on purpose (ext-session-lock has the same rule), and KWin maintainers are unlikely to accept it; the 2 s stuck/crashed-greeter fallback makes it worse. It also only shrinks the black: the after media still show ~0.2 s of black and the clock fading in on black, because the slow part (greeter start, QML, wallpaper decoded only after expose, 800 ms launch fade) is untouched.
changes: Drop the KWin render-loop hold; keep blanking as soon as the session is locked.

Fix the latency in kscreenlocker/plasma-workspace instead: decode the lock wallpaper before (or as) the greeter window is first shown and hold the LockScreenUi fade until the wallpaper is loaded, so the first visible frame is the full lock screen.
If a further cut is wanted, look at the greeter startup itself (pre-starting the greeter or a pre-scaled cached lock wallpaper) rather than showing unlocked content.
